questions.q: Which gland is shown in this slide?
questions.explain: Follicles filled with colloid and lined by a single layer of cells are the visible clue.
questions.alt: Round follicles of different sizes are filled with smooth pink-orange material and lined by small dark-nucleated cells.

questions.q: What fills the follicles in this slide?
questions.explain: Colloid is the stored form of thyroid hormone precursor.
questions.alt: Round follicles of different sizes are filled with smooth pink-orange material and lined by small dark-nucleated cells.

questions.q: Which cells lie between follicles and secrete calcitonin?
questions.explain: C cells sit between follicles or at their edge and secrete calcitonin.
questions.alt: Round follicles of different sizes are filled with smooth pink-orange material and lined by small dark-nucleated cells.

questions.q: Which histological feature is most characteristic of the adrenal cortex?
options: Cells arranged in cords or clusters around sinusoidal capillaries
Colloid-filled follicles lined by simple cuboidal epithelium
questions.explain: The adrenal cortex is composed of steroid-secreting cells arranged in zones and cords separated by fenestrated sinusoidal capillaries.

questions.q: A section of adrenal gland shows cells in rounded clusters with a foamy, lipid-rich cytoplasm in the outer cortical zone. Which hormone is principally produced by this zone?
questions.explain: The zona glomerulosa is the outermost adrenal cortical zone and synthesises mineralocorticoids, chiefly aldosterone.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes the zona fasciculata from the zona glomerulosa in an adrenal histology slide?
options: Long straight cords of pale, lipid-rich spongiocytes
Chief cells arranged around parathyroid capillaries
questions.explain: The zona fasciculata is the broad middle cortical zone. Its lipid-rich spongiocytes form long cords separated by sinusoidal capillaries.

questions.q: A histological section shows the inner adrenal cortex with smaller eosinophilic cells arranged in branching networks. Which product is most associated with this zone?
questions.explain: The zona reticularis is the innermost cortical zone and contributes adrenal androgens, including dehydroepiandrosterone and its sulfate.

questions.q: A section of adrenal medulla shows large polygonal cells closely associated with sinusoidal capillaries. What is the embryological origin of these secretory cells?
questions.explain: Adrenal medullary chromaffin cells are modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons derived from neural crest cells.

questions.q: A histological section of the anterior pituitary shows acidophils and basophils arranged in cords around sinusoidal capillaries. Which cell group includes the growth hormone-secreting somatotrophs?
questions.explain: Somatotrophs are acidophils of the pars distalis; they secrete growth hormone. Basophils include corticotrophs, thyrotrophs and gonadotrophs, while pituicytes are glial cells of the posterior pituitary.

questions.q: A pituitary section contains pale-staining cells with few visible secretory granules. Which interpretation of these chromophobes is most appropriate?
options: They may represent degranulated chromophils or undifferentiated cells
They are the hormone-storing axon terminals of the posterior pituitary
They are endothelial cells lining the sinusoids
questions.explain: Chromophobes stain weakly because they contain few visible secretory granules; many are degranulated chromophils, although some may be undifferentiated cells.

questions.q: A parathyroid section from an adult shows numerous small, chief cells and scattered larger cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. What are the larger cells called?
questions.explain: Oxyphil cells are larger, strongly eosinophilic parathyroid cells with abundant mitochondria. Chief cells are the principal source of parathyroid hormone.

questions.q: A thyroid follicle is lined by tall columnar follicular cells and contains scalloped colloid at its edge. What does this appearance most strongly indicate?
options: Active synthesis and resorption of thyroid hormone
questions.explain: Tall follicular epithelium and scalloping of colloid reflect active colloid endocytosis and thyroid hormone production/release. Flattened epithelium with abundant smooth colloid is more typical of an inactive gland.

questions.q: In a routine histological section of the pancreas, which feature best distinguishes an islet of Langerhans from the surrounding exocrine acini?
options: A duct lined by stratified squamous epithelium
A pale-staining cluster of endocrine cells richly supplied by capillaries
A central lumen containing zymogen granules
A capsule of dense irregular connective tissue
questions.explain: Pancreatic islets appear as pale-staining endocrine cell clusters with a rich fenestrated capillary network; exocrine acini are darker and organised around small lumina.
